title: How Motivation Really Works
desc: Some mornings you leap out of bed, and some mornings you can't move at all. Why? In this calm, sourced deep dive we follow motivation from the inside: why monkeys solved puzzles for no reward, what dopamine really does (wanting is not liking), why a reward can quietly make a fun thing less fun, what people actually need, why choice and a sense of control matter, how goals help and when they backfire, why progress feels so good, what the marshmallow test and the willpower debate really showed, why we procrastinate, how habits take over, and where flow and meaning come in. Every claim comes from named studies, with the doubts left in. At the end there is a slow, gentle wind-down, so you can listen until you drift off.
plan: b01: hook (the alarm goes off; some mornings you leap up, some you can't move) + 'Tonight, we'll explore' list + motivation as the force that turns wanting into doing; open loop: how a reward can make a fun thing less fun (paid off b06); no money examples

b02: drives and curiosity: Cannon 1932 homeostasis; Hull 1943 drive reduction; Harlow, Harlow & Meyer 1950 monkeys solved puzzles with no reward; Berlyne 1960 curiosity; Yerkes & Dodson 1908 and why the inverted U is overused

b03: wanting vs liking: Olds & Milner 1954 rats pressing a lever; Schultz, Dayan & Montague 1997 reward prediction error; Berridge & Robinson 1998 wanting is not liking; Salamone & Correa 2012 dopamine and effort; why anticipation can beat the thing itself

b04: rewards and schedules: Thorndike 1898 puzzle boxes, law of effect; Skinner and Ferster & Skinner 1957 schedules of reinforcement; variable rewards and why checking feels compulsive; Hull 1932 goal gradient in rats; Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006 coffee stamp card (head start: 2 of 12 pre-stamped vs 0 of 10)

b05: needs: Maslow 1943, and the pyramid he never drew (Bridgman, Cummings & Ballard 2019); Tay & Diener 2011 needs and wellbeing across 123 countries; Murray 1938 list of needs; McClelland need for achievement; Baumeister & Leary 1995 need to belong

b06: the overjustification effect (pays off the b01 loop): Deci 1971 Soma puzzles; Lepper, Greene & Nisbett 1973 children's drawing with markers and the Good Player Award; Deci, Koestner & Ryan 1999 meta-analysis (expected tangible rewards undermine, unexpected and verbal praise do not); Cameron & Pierce 1994 counterpoint; Henderlong & Lepper 2002 praise

b07: self-determination theory: Ryan & Deci 2000 autonomy, competence, relatedness; Langer & Rodin 1976 nursing home plants and choice; Iyengar & Lepper 2000 jam study and Scheibehenne, Greifeneder & Todd 2010 meta-analysis (average effect near zero); Patall, Cooper & Robinson 2008 choice meta-analysis

b08: goals: Locke & Latham 2002 specific hard goals; Ordonez et al. 2009 'Goals gone wild' caveat; Oettingen positive fantasies (Kappes & Oettingen 2011, lower energy); mental contrasting / WOOP (Oettingen 2014); Gollwitzer 1999 and Gollwitzer & Sheeran 2006 implementation intentions

b09: progress: Zeigarnik 1927 unfinished tasks (mixed replications) and Ovsiankina 1928 resumption; Amabile & Kramer 2011 progress principle (diaries of 238 workers); Koo & Fishbach 2008 focus on done vs left; Bonezzi, Brendl & De Angelis 2011 stuck in the middle

b10: self-control: Mischel, Ebbesen & Zeiss 1972 marshmallow and strategies (distraction); Shoda, Mischel & Peake 1990 follow-up; Watts, Duncan & Quan 2018 replication (smaller link); Kidd, Palmeri & Aslin 2013 reliable vs unreliable adult; Baumeister et al. 1998 radishes and ego depletion; Hagger et al. 2016 registered replication (near zero); Job, Dweck & Walton 2010 beliefs about willpower

b11: procrastination: Steel 2007 meta-analysis (temporal motivation); Tice & Baumeister 1997 students; Sirois & Pychyl 2013 mood repair; Pronin, Olivola & Kennedy 2008 future self treated like another person (the disgusting drink); Ersner-Hershfield et al. 2009 future self in the brain; Wohl, Pychyl & Bennett 2010 self-forgiveness

b12: belief and expectancy: Bandura 1977 self-efficacy; Seligman & Maier 1967 learned helplessness and Maier & Seligman 2016 revision; Dweck growth mindset; Sisk et al. 2018 meta-analyses (small effects); Yeager et al. 2019 national study (small, larger for lower-achieving students)

b13: other people: Triplett 1898 cyclists and fishing reels; Zajonc 1965 social facilitation; Ringelmann rope pulling, Latane, Williams & Harkins 1979 clapping and social loafing; Kohler effect (Kerr & Hertel 2011); Goldstein, Cialdini & Griskevicius 2008 hotel towels and social norms

b14: habits: Wood, Quinn & Kashy 2002 (about 43% of daily actions repeated in the same context); Lally et al. 2010 (median 66 days, range 18 to 254; the 21-day myth from Maltz 1960); Neal, Wood, Wu & Kurlander 2011 stale popcorn; Milkman, Minson & Volpp 2014 temptation bundling (audiobooks at the gym); Wood & Neal 2007 cues

b15: flow and meaning: Csikszentmihalyi 1975 and 1990 flow; experience sampling (Csikszentmihalyi & LeFevre 1989 'paradox of work'); Frankl 1946; Wrzesniewski et al. 1997 jobs, careers, callings; Ariely, Kamenica & Prelec 2008 Lego Bionicles (seen vs shredded work, no pay amounts mentioned)

b16: starting again: fresh start effect (Dai, Milkman & Riis 2014); the what-the-hell effect (Polivy & Herman 1985, Cochran & Tesser 1996); rest and motivation; callback to the alarm clock; recap of the whole night
b17: guided wind-down: nothing to achieve tonight, the breath, a slow walk along a quiet path, letting the day's to-do list fade, goodnight, end segment teasing 'How Your Brain Makes Decisions'
